key_insight: A founder loss-of-function variant in UBE2L3 was enriched in Arab ICU sepsis cases, suggesting UBE2L3 may influence sepsis susceptibility and be a potential therapeutic target.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this finding could help guide genetic risk stratification and prioritize UBE2L3-focused drug discovery for sepsis.
method: WGS-based GWAS and exome-wide association analysis in 210 Arab ICU patients
Prioritized deleterious founder variants using REGENIE Firth regression, CADD, and allele-frequency enrichment
Followed up UBE2L3 signals in All of Us and supported target relevance with AI drug-development scoring
evidence_signal: The strongest case-control signal was a novel UBE2L3 start-loss variant seen in 3/68 sepsis cases and 0/142 controls, with supportive association for UBE2L3 missense burden in All of Us bacterial infection data.
watch_item: The UBE2L3 findings are based on small case numbers and broad confidence intervals, so independent replication and functional validation are needed before translation.
paper_title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Sepsis Susceptibility in ICU Patients Identifies Arab Founder Loss-of-Function Variant in UBE2L3
